The eldest child of Alfred the Great, this Anglo-Saxon noblewoman ruled the Mercians in her own right from 911 until her death in 918 — who was she?
Æthelflæd: Ruler of Mercia in England from 911 to 918.

Pascal (programming language) (published 1972) is the earliest of the four.

What is the atomic number of Zirconium?
Zirconium is a chemical element; it has symbol Zr and atomic number 40.
What is the atomic number of Francium?
Francium is a chemical element; it has symbol Fr and atomic number 87.
In what year was Ursula von der Leyen born?
Ursula von der Leyen: Von der Leyen was born and raised in Brussels, Belgium, to German parents.
In what year was Factitious disorder imposed on another discovered?
Factitious disorder imposed on another: The victim is typically the caregiver's child but is occasionally an adult partner.
In what year was Iridium discovered?
Iridium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ir and atomic number 77.

Mitsubishi A6M Zero: Japan. It was operated by the Imperial Japanese Navy (IJN) from 1940 to 1945.
Who is credited with discovering Eta Carinae?
Eta Carinae: Pieter Dirkszoon Keyser. It became the second-brightest star in the night sky between 11–14 March 1843 before fading well below naked-eye visibility after 1856.
Who is credited with discovering Benzene?
Benzene: Michael Faraday. Benzene is an organic chemical compound with the molecular formula C6H6.
Who is credited with discovering Vanadium?
Vanadium: Andrés Manuel del Río. Vanadium is a chemical element; it has symbol V and atomic number 23.

This mosquito species, native to tropical Southeast Asia and marked with distinctive white bands on its legs and body, has spread worldwide via international trade and travel, becoming a significant public health concern — what species is it?

Aedes albopictus (synonym Stegomyia albopicta), from the mosquito (Culicidae) family, also known as the (Asian) tiger mosquito or forest mosquito, is a species of mosquito native to the tropical and subtropical areas of Southeast Asia.

This central nervous system stimulant treats ADHD and narcolepsy today, but was once prescribed for nasal congestion and depression, and remains tightly controlled due to its abuse potential — name the drug?

Amphetamine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant that is used in the treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and narcolepsy; it is also used to treat binge eating disorder in the form of lisdexamfetamine.
Native to Europe but introduced to North America, this orb-weaver spider species is known by several common names, one of them shared confusingly with a different species — which species?
Araneus diadematus is commonly called the European garden spider, cross orbweaver, diadem spider, orangie, cross spider, and crowned orb weaver.
This American physicist shared the 2017 Nobel with Rainer Weiss and Kip Thorne for decisive contributions to LIGO and the observation of gravitational waves — who is he?
Barry Barish (born January 27, 1936) is an American experimental physicist and Nobel Laureate.
Despite its name, this sub-Saharan snake is actually grey to dark brown — the second-longest venomous snake in the world after the king cobra, commonly reaching 3 meters — name this species?
Black mamba (Dendroaspis polylepis) is a species of highly venomous snake belonging to the family Elapidae.
Also known as undulant fever and Malta fever, this zoonotic illness spreads mainly through drinking unpasteurized milk and is caused by tiny coccobacilli — what is it?
Brucellosis is a zoonosis (zoonotic disease) spread primarily via ingestion of unpasteurized milk from infected animals.
This medical specialty diagnoses and treats congenital heart defects, valvular disease, and heart failure, and is a sub-specialty of internal medicine — which field?
Cardiology (from Ancient Greek (kardi) 'heart' and - (-logia) 'study') is the study of the heart.

This compound is a yellowish-green gas above 11°C, a reddish-brown liquid when cooler, and bright orange crystals when very cold — usually handled in solution as a bleach and disinfectant. What is it?

Chlorine dioxide is a chemical compound with the formula ClO2 that exists as yellowish-green gas above 11 C (52 F), a reddish-brown liquid between 11 and 59 C (52 and 74 F), and as bright orange crystals below 59 C (74 F).
In mathematics, this term describes a selection of items from a set in which the order of choosing doesn't matter — unlike its counterpart, the permutation. Name the concept?
Combination is a selection of items from a set that has distinct members, such that the order of selection does not matter (unlike permutations).

Named for a mythological Greek youth who was transformed into a tree after accidentally killing a beloved stag, this genus of evergreen conifers is considered polyphyletic by modern genetic analysis — what genus is it?
Cupressus (common name cypress) is one of several genera of evergreen conifers within the family Cupressaceae; for the others, see cypress.

This is the practice of communication between representatives of states or institutions aimed at influencing international events, serving as the main instrument through which foreign policy goals are pursued. What is this practice called?
Diplomacy is the communication by representatives of state, intergovernmental, or non-governmental institutions intended to influence events in the international system.
In 2009 she became the first woman to win the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, honored for her analysis of how communities govern shared commons — which political economist was she?

Elinor Ostrom (ne Awan; August 7, 1933 - June 12, 2012) was an American political scientist and political economist whose work was associated with New Institutional Economics and the resurgence of political economy.
Botanists use this word for any plant whose leaves stay green and functional through every season, never going bare like a deciduous tree — what is it?
Evergreen is a plant which has foliage that remains green and functional throughout the year.
Sharing the 1962 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Maurice Wilkins, this English molecular biologist helped decipher the structure of DNA — who is he?
Francis Crick (8 June 1916 - 28 July 2004) was an English molecular biologist, biophysicist, and neuroscientist.
This pancreatic hormone kicks in when blood sugar dips too low, prompting the liver to convert stored glycogen back into glucose. What is it?
Glucagon is a peptide hormone, produced by alpha cells of the pancreas.
Newborns with this severe genetic skin disorder are born encased in thick, diamond-shaped plates separated by deep cracks that restrict movement and breathing — what is it?
Harlequin-type ichthyosis is a genetic disorder that results in thickened skin over nearly the entire body at birth.

Which field of study leans on anthropology, paleontology, and genetics to trace how our ancestors gradually picked up bipedalism, dexterity, and complex language — a story that turned out to be weblike rather than a tidy straight line?
Human evolution is a distinct species of the hominid family of primates, which includes all the great apes.
Denoted by the symbol ∞, this concept of the boundless and endless has been debated by philosophers since ancient Greece and by mathematicians since the 17th century — what is it?
Infinity is something which is boundless, limitless, or endless.
This German polymath wrote The Sorrows of Young Werther and essays on botany, anatomy, and color theory—he's the most influential writer in the German language. Who was he?
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (28 August 1749 - 22 March 1832) was a German polymath who is widely regarded as the most influential writer in the German language.
First described in 1816 and classed in psychiatry as an impulse-control disorder, this condition is the inability to resist stealing items one doesn't even need — what's its name?
Kleptomania is the inability to resist the urge to steal items, usually for reasons other than personal use or financial gain.
Found in the support tissues of most plants, this polymer resists rot and reinforces wood and bark structure — what is it?
Lignin is a class of complex organic polymers that form key structural materials in the support tissues of most plants.
This genus of Old World monkeys includes 23 species ranging from Asia and North Africa all the way to Gibraltar, and mostly eats fruit — what is it?
Macaque (Macaca) of gregarious Old World monkeys of the subfamily Cercopithecinae.
This small southern-African mongoose has digging foreclaws and a knack for thermoregulating in harsh, dry country, living in tight packs of up to 30 — which sharp-eyed animal is it?
Meerkat (Suricata suricatta) or suricate is a small mongoose found in southern Africa.
The dried leaves of this Southeast Asian evergreen tree, known as kratom, contain alkaloids that bind to opioid receptors as partial agonists. What plant is it?
Mitragyna speciosa is a tropical evergreen tree of the Rubiaceae family native to Southeast Asia.
The paranasal sinuses all drain into this air-filled space that channels inhaled air from the nostrils down toward the throat — what is it?
Nasal cavity is an air-filled space above and behind the nose in the middle of the face.
This massive bony fish, weighing up to a metric ton, resembles a giant fish head without a tail and is native to tropical and temperate waters worldwide. What is it?
Ocean sunfish (Mola mola), also known as the common mola, is one of the largest bony fish in the world.

Nicknamed the 'white rats' of its phylum for how often it's used in classroom and lab experiments, this single-celled ciliate thrives in freshwater, brackish, and marine habitats — what organism is it?
Paramecium ((ee-)m, -see-m, plural "paramecia" only when used as a vernacular name) is a genus of eukaryotic, unicellular ciliates, widespread in freshwater, brackish, and marine environments.
This herbaceous annual vine produces edible pods and comes in bush or climbing cultivars; global output hit 28 million tonnes in 2022, led by India. What legume species is it?
Phaseolus vulgaris is a herbaceous annual plant. Its botanical classification, along with other Phaseolus species, is as a member of the legume family, Fabaceae.

This medical condition occurs when air collects in the space between the lung and chest wall, typically causing sudden, sharp one-sided chest pain and shortness of breath — what's the condition called?
Pneumothorax is collection of air in the pleural space between the lung and the chest wall.

Named early in the history of microbiology for its widespread presence in water and plant seeds, which genus of gram-negative bacteria includes an opportunistic human pathogen infamous in hospitals as well as plant and soil-dwelling species?
Pseudomonas is a genus of gram-negative bacteria belonging to the family Pseudomonadaceae in the class Gammaproteobacteria.
What fat-soluble alcohol form of vitamin A — found in fish, dairy, and meat — is essential for vision, skin maintenance, and immune function, and is used as a supplement to prevent xerophthalmia?
Retinol is a hydrolytic metabolite of retinyl esters belonging to the group of vitamin A1 as an alcohol form.

These lizard-like amphibians, grouped in the order Urodela, keep a tail throughout both their larval and adult life stages — unlike their tailless amphibian cousins the frogs and toads. What animal is it?

Salamander are a group of amphibians typically characterized by their lizard-like appearance, with slender bodies, blunt snouts, short limbs projecting at right angles to the body, and the presence of a tail in both larvae and adults.
This Pakistani-American businessman owns both an NFL franchise, the Jacksonville Jaguars, and an English Premier League club, Fulham — who is he?
Shahid Khan (born July 18, 1950) is a Pakistani and American businessman.
This circular muscle normally maintains constriction of a natural body passage, relaxing only as physiological function requires — what is it called?
Sphincter is a circular muscle that normally maintains constriction of a natural body passage or orifice and relaxes as required by normal physiological functioning.
Encompassing domestic pigs and their ancestor the Eurasian wild boar, this genus within the even-toed ungulate family Suidae is native across Eurasia and Africa — which genus?

Sus (genus) is the genus of domestic and wild pigs, within the even-toed ungulate family Suidae. Sus includes domestic pigs (Sus domesticus) and their ancestor, the common Eurasian wild boar (Sus scrofa), along with various other species.
A European Space Agency astronaut who is also a musician and writer, this Frenchman logged two six-month stints aboard the ISS, the second launched via SpaceX Crew Dragon in 2021 — who is he?
Thomas Pesquet (French; born 27 February 1978, is a French aerospace engineer, pilot, European Space Agency astronaut, actor, musician, and writer.
Egypt and Iraq both flew this Soviet-designed jet bomber in wars against Israel, and China still produces an updated license-built version, the H-6K — which aircraft?
Tupolev Tu-16 (USAF/DOD reporting name Type 39; NATO reporting name: Badger) is a twin-engined jet strategic heavy bomber used by the Soviet Union.

Belonging to the same family as kangaroos, this informally named group of smaller macropods is native to Australia and New Guinea, with introduced populations as far away as Hawaii and the UK — what are they called?
Wallaby is a small or middle-sized macropod native to Australia and New Guinea, with introduced populations in New Zealand, Hawaii, the United Kingdom and other countries.
A white, water-insoluble powder with the formula ZnO, this compound turns up in everything from sunscreens and calamine lotion to batteries and semiconductors — name this compound?
Zinc oxide is an inorganic compound with the formula ZnO. Although it occurs naturally as the mineral zincite, most zinc oxide is produced synthetically.
Made by the adrenal glands, this hormone powers the fight-or-flight response — boosting blood flow to muscles, dilating pupils and raising blood sugar by hitting alpha and beta receptors. What is it?
Adrenaline: Hormone and medication. It appears as a white microcrystalline granule.
This Austrian psychotherapist broke from Freud's circle to found 'individual psychology,' emphasizing birth order and coining the term 'inferiority complex' — who was he?
First identified as a chemical in 1887 and later marketed as the drug Benzedrine, this CNS stimulant is prescribed today for ADHD and narcolepsy — which drug?
Nicknamed 'Nastia' in the USSR and known to NATO as 'Curl,' this twin-engine turboprop military transport was later license-built in China under a different name — what aircraft is it?
Antonov An-26: Soviet turboprop transport aircraft. It is the third member of the Antonov An-24 family, coming after the An-24 and An-30, while preceding the An-32 and cancelled An-132.
Ranking as the second-largest lizard species after the Komodo dragon, this excellent swimmer thrives in lakes, rivers, and even city sewers across South and Southeast Asia — what is it?
Asian water monitor: Species of lizard. The Asian water monitor (Varanus salvator) is a large varanid lizard native to South and Southeast Asia.
This fig tree spreads outward indefinitely by growing extra trunks from its own prop roots, and its most famous species is the national tree of India — what is it?
This red-orange breakdown product of heme colors feces brown and urine pale yellow as it's further broken down in the body — which compound?
Bilirubin: Red pigment of the bile.

A twin-engine, carrier-capable strike fighter flown by the U.S., Australia, and Kuwait, this larger, more advanced follow-on to an earlier 1980s Navy jet packs an internal 20 mm rotary cannon and can be rigged as an airborne refueling tanker — what is it called?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Boeing F/A-18E/F Super Hornet: Series of carrier-based multirole combat aircraft.
Despite the name, this pseudocereal isn't related to true cereals at all — it's kin to rhubarb and sorrel, and was first cultivated in Yunnan around 6,000 BC — which crop is it?
Buckwheat: Species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae.
This highly contagious virus, spread through feces, can kill up to 91% of untreated dogs and wolves and also strikes foxes, cats, and skunks — what is it?
Canine parvovirus: Contagious virus mainly affecting dogs.
Native to Madagascar, this flowering plant known as the Madagascar periwinkle is the source of two major cancer-fighting drugs — what is it?
Catharanthus roseus: Species of flowering plant in the family Apocynaceae.
Caused by a member of the herpesvirus family, this airborne illness usually starts on the chest, back, and face before the itchy little blisters scab over all over the body — what is it?
Sold under the brand name Klonopin, this long-acting benzodiazepine kicks in within an hour and lasts eight to twelve, treating anxiety, seizures, and panic — which drug is it?
Clonazepam: Benzodiazepine medication. It possesses anxiolytic, anticonvulsant, sedative, hypnotic, and skeletal muscle relaxant properties.

Nicknamed the deaf adder or long-cripple in parts of Europe, this legless, burrowing lizard has smooth scales that don't overlap — and despite its name, it's neither a snake nor what it sounds like. What is it?
Common slow worm: Species of legless lizard. The common slow worm (Anguis fragilis) is a non-venomous species of legless lizard native to Europe.
Found in the tropics of Africa, Asia, the Americas, and Australia, this large semiaquatic reptile congregates in rivers and wetlands and is closely related to alligators and caimans — what is it?
Crocodile: Family of large reptilian carnivores.
This Manhattan Project physicist later led the Federation of American Scientists and is best remembered for his 1959 Senate testimony opposing Lewis Strauss's Commerce nomination — who is he?
David L. Hill: American nuclear physicist (1919–2008)
Named for the unique double-beamed bones under its tail, this long-necked Jurassic giant is one of the most common fossils found in North America's Morrison Formation. What dinosaur is it?
Diplodocus: Genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaurs (fossil)
This condition involves involuntarily repeating words or sounds spoken by someone else, and is commonly seen in autism, ADHD, and Tourette syndrome. What is it called?

This is the process of creating economic value by spotting and commercializing opportunities — typically demanding considerable initiative and bearing real risk in exchange for most of the reward. What's the term?
Entrepreneurship: Taking financial risks in the hope of profit.
Also known by the scientific name Gyps fulvus, this large Old World bird of prey belongs to the family Accipitridae — which species is it?
Eurasian griffon vulture: Species of bird. It is also known as the Eurasian griffon or griffon vulture, although the latter term is sometimes used for the genus Gyps as a whole.
This centuries-old number theory statement claims there are no positive whole-number solutions to a^n + b^n = c^n whenever the exponent exceeds two — what's it called?
Fermat's Last Theorem: 17th-century conjecture proved by Andrew Wiles in 1994.
This American chemical engineer at Caltech won the 2018 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for pioneering 'directed evolution' to engineer enzymes — and later joined Alphabet's board — who is it?
Frances Arnold: American chemist and academic (born 1956)
Once Mexico's top law-enforcement official as secretary of public security, this man was convicted in a Brooklyn courtroom in 2023 for taking millions in bribes from the Sinaloa Cartel — who is he?
Genaro García Luna: Mexican politician and convicted felon (born 1968)
With the symbol Au and atomic number 79, this soft, dense element is so unreactive that only platinum sits below it — and it often turns up as native nuggets in riverbeds. What is it?
Gold: Chemical element with atomic number 79 (Au). Chemically, gold is a transition metal, a group 11 element, and one of the noble metals.

Named from Greek words meaning 'naked seed,' this group of woody plants — including conifers, cycads, and ginkgos — lacks the protective covering that encloses a flowering plant's seeds. What is it called?
Gymnosperm: Clade of non-flowering, naked-seeded vascular plants.

Often triggered by a preceding throat infection, this childhood autoimmune disease causes raised skin bruising, joint pain, and sometimes kidney trouble from IgA immune-complex deposits — what is it called?
Henoch–Schönlein purpura: Autoimmune vascular inflammatory disease.
Defined today as exactly 3,600 seconds, this unit of time was originally a variable measure equal to one-twelfth of the night or day in the ancient Near East — which unit?
Hour: Unit of time equal to 60 minutes.

Once diagnosed almost exclusively in women during the 19th century and studied intensely by Sigmund Freud and Jean-Martin Charcot, this term for 'ungovernable emotional excess' is no longer accepted as a medical diagnosis. What is it called?
Hysteria: Excess, ungovernable emotion. Hysteria is a term used to mean ungovernable emotional excess and can refer to a temporary state of mind or emotion.

He won the 1944 Nobel Prize for his resonance method of recording the magnetic properties of atomic nuclei, and was among the first Americans to work on the cavity magnetron behind radar and microwave ovens — which physicist?
This German craftsman's mechanical printing press — with its oil-based ink and adjustable metal type — sparked an information revolution that helped fuel the Renaissance and Reformation — who is he?
Johannes Gutenberg: German inventor and craftsman (c. 1393–1406 – 1468)
Named from a Tongan and Marquesan word meaning 'bitter,' this pepper-family plant's ground root becomes a ceremonial Pacific Islands drink that numbs the mouth — what is it?
Kava: Species of plant. Kava or kava kava (Piper methysticum: Latin 'pepper' and Latinized Greek 'intoxicating') is a plant in the pepper family, native to the Pacific Islands.
A genus of 47 flowering plant species in the sage family, prized for its fragrant oil and used in traditional medicine, cosmetics, and as a culinary herb across Mediterranean climates — which genus?
Lavandula: Genus of plants. Lavandula (common name lavender) is a genus of 47 known species of perennial flowering plants in the sage family, Lamiaceae.
Also known as the deer ked, this blood-sucking fly sheds its own wings once it lands on a host and burrows through the fur to feed — what species is it?
Lipoptena cervi: Species of fly. Lipoptena cervi, the deer ked or deer fly, is a species of biting fly in the family of louse flies, Hippoboscidae.
Often a complication of cancer treatment, this incurable, progressive swelling condition is managed with compression therapy and manual drainage rather than diuretics — what is it?
Lymphedema: Swelling due to a compromised lymphatic system.

The first woman to write a mathematics handbook and the first appointed as a university math professor, this Milanese scholar later traded calculus for four decades of theology and charity — who is she?
Maria Gaetana Agnesi: Italian mathematician and philanthropist (1718–1799)
Comprising 18 to 24 species that hybridize freely where their ranges overlap, this genus of the mint family thrives in wet, moist soils worldwide — what is it?
Mentha: Genus of flowering plants in the family Lamiaceae.

Given the NATO reporting name 'Hip,' this Soviet-designed helicopter family has been in continuous production since 1975 as a medium twin-turbine transport, with an armed gunship variant — which aircraft?
Mil Mi-17: Family of Russian military transport helicopters.
Built with a slender segmented body and a long piercing-and-sucking proboscis, this family of 3,600 fly species diversified back in the Cretaceous — what are they?
Mosquito: Family of flies. The word mosquito (formed by mosca and diminutive -ito) is Spanish and Portuguese for little fly.

This branch of alternative medicine rests on vitalism and folk healing rather than evidence, and its grab-bag of 'natural' methods runs from the thoroughly discredited to certain accepted psychotherapies. What is it?
Naturopathy: Form of alternative medicine. The ethics of naturopathy have been called into question by medical professionals and its practice has been characterized as quackery.

The first of the Century Series jet fighters, this supersonic aircraft was the U.S. Air Force's first fighter capable of level supersonic flight, first taking to the air in May 1953, seven months ahead of schedule — which jet?

North American F-100 Super Sabre: 1953 fighter aircraft family. The North American F-100 Super Sabre is an American supersonic jet fighter aircraft designed and produced by the aircraft manufacturer North American Aviation.

The world's most widespread and commercially important cactus species, this domesticated crop is grown both as a fruit and for its edible vegetable pads, likely originating in central Mexico — which species?
Opuntia ficus-indica: Species of cactus. It is grown primarily as a fruit crop, and also for the vegetable nopales and other uses.
Commonly known as the bullet ant for its notoriously painful sting, which insect species inhabits the humid lowland rainforests of Central and South America?
Often triggered by a ruptured appendix or a perforated gallbladder, this inflammation of the abdominal lining causes severe pain and swelling — what is it?

Peritonitis: Inflammation of abdominal organ lining. Peritonitis is inflammation of the localized or generalized peritoneum, the lining of the inner wall of the abdomen and covering of the abdominal organs.
Resembling a round, tailless rabbit with short ears, this small mountain-dwelling mammal's Himalayan relative lives at elevations above 6,000 meters — what animal is it?
Pika: Genus of mountain-dwelling mammal. A pika ( PY-kə, PEE-kə) is a small, mountain-dwelling mammal native to Asia and North America.
This succulent plant in the family Portulacaceae has every part edible, whether raw or cooked, and is also known by folk names like little hogweed — what is it, scientifically speaking?
Portulaca oleracea: Species of plant in the purslane family.
Which medical specialty focuses on diagnosing, treating, and preventing conditions related to cognition, mood, emotion, and behavior, using tools like the DSM-5?
Psychiatry: Branch of medicine devoted to mental disorders.
Native to Southeast Asia and a close relative of the lychee and longan, this medium-sized tree lends its name to a hairy-skinned tropical fruit — what is it?
Rambutan: Southeast Asian fruit. Rambutan (Nephelium lappaceum) is a medium-sized tropical tree in the family Sapindaceae.
Extracted from the seeds of the castor oil plant, this lectin toxin carries an estimated lethal oral dose in humans of about one milligram per kilogram — what is it?
Belonging to the order Urodela and reaching their greatest diversity in the Appalachian Mountains, these tailed, lizard-shaped amphibians never have more than four front toes — what are they?
Salamander: Order of amphibians. All ten extant salamander families are grouped together under the order Urodela, the sole surviving order from the group Caudata.
These marine algae include the kelps that shelter fisheries and are estimated to produce at least half of Earth's oxygen — what are they collectively called?
Seaweed: Macroscopic marine algae. Seaweed, or macroalgae, refers to thousands of species of macroscopic, multicellular, marine algae.
This order of fully aquatic, herbivorous mammals includes dugongs and manatees and is more closely related to elephants than to whales — what is it called?
Sirenia: Order of aquatic herbivorous mammals. The Protosirenidae (Eocene sirenians) and Prorastomidae (terrestrial sirenians) families are extinct.
With eight legs, venom-injecting fangs, and silk-spinning spinnerets, this arthropod has spread to every continent but Antarctica — over 53,000 species and counting. What is it?
Signified by the minus sign, this arithmetic operation represents removing objects from a collection and is the inverse of addition — which operation is it?
Subtraction: One of the four basic arithmetic operations.
This genus of flowering plants, commonly called dandelions, thrives nearly worldwide in yards, gardens, and roadsides — which genus?
Taraxacum: Genus of flowering plants in the family Asteraceae.
Working in his famous "Fly Room" with fruit flies, this American won a Nobel for showing that genes ride on chromosomes — who was he?
Commonly nicknamed a "mini-stroke," this brief disruption of blood flow to the brain causes stroke-like symptoms that fully resolve within 24 hours — what medical event is it?
Transient ischemic attack: Minor form of stroke.
This group of large hoofed mammals splits into odd-toed members like horses and rhinos, and even-toed members like cattle, giraffes, and camels — what are they called?
Ungulate: Group of mammals that walk on the tips of their toes or hooves.

This Soviet cosmonaut commanded the first spaceflight to carry more than one crew member in 1964, then became the first human to die during a space mission when his parachute failed in 1967 — who was he?
Also called a slater or sow bug depending on region, this terrestrial crustacean is one of the few crustacean lineages to fully colonize dry land — what is it?
